title: Choose the product detail structure
question: Which page structure best helps a shopper assess a product from its documented information?

options.label: Image-led summary
options.lineage: A split product overview with details continuing below.
options.thesis: Let the product image and a concise, complete summary share the first read.
options.viewport: A single API image leads on the left; product name, category, API price, stock, quantity, and the conditional cart action align on the right. Description and other documented fields continue below.
options.risk: The split can narrow the description column; preserve a readable single-column sequence on compact screens.

regions.label: Name, price, stock, quantity, cart action

options.label: Image with purchase rail
options.lineage: A broad product image paired with a narrow action rail.
options.thesis: Keep the product visible while the purchase controls stay in one predictable place.
options.viewport: Product identity and category sit above a wide single-image area; a narrow rail carries API price, stock, quantity, and the conditional cart action. Description, store, and tags follow as unboxed text.
options.risk: A narrow action rail can feel cramped at mid-size widths; let the image and action area stack before either becomes compressed.

options.label: Product information sheet
options.lineage: A field-led product record with the image as one part of the overview.
options.thesis: Make documented product facts easy to scan before the shopper commits.
options.viewport: A full-width name and category introduce a two-column record: description and ruled API fields on one side, a single image and price/stock/quantity action on the other.
options.risk: A field list can overemphasize metadata; keep the product name and image prominent and omit fields the API does not provide.
